story: The barred spiral galaxy NGC 4519 features in this small section of one of the First Look images from the NSF–DOE Vera C. Rubin Observatory. Directly above it sits its companion, a lenticular galaxy called PGC 41706. NGC 4519 lies about 55 million light-years away, in the direction of Virgo.

A barred spiral has a straight bar of stars running through its center, with spiral arms winding out from the ends of the bar. A lenticular galaxy has a disk like a spiral but lacks prominent arms. Neighboring galaxies like these can influence each other through gravity over long periods, tugging on stars and gas.

This view comes from Rubin's LSST Camera on the Simonyi Survey Telescope, which combined exposures through u, g, r and i filters. Stacking many exposures reveals faint detail that a single short look would miss.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (9.82 x 9.82 arcminutes) and distance (55 million light years), the frame spans roughly 157,000 × 157,000 light-years. Its light set out about 55 million years before reaching the telescope.
